interactions.note: The epitope specific single domain VHH affinity matured cAb-RN05 (clone a) was analyzed for binding using a yeast surface display system and measured by flow cytometry. Alanine scanning mutagenesis of clone a identified five residues that contributed to enhanced binding in the affinity-matured antibody.

The epitope specific single domain VHH camel antibody RN05 was analyzed for binding using a yeast surface display system and measured by flow cytometry. Alanine scanning mutagenesis of the antibody CDR1 and CDR3 regions revealed three critical side chain residues that make direct contact with RNase A and four other positions important for backbone-mediated interactions. CDR2 residues were not examined because none of them make direct contacts with the antigen.
The Kd value for the epitope specific VHH cAb-RN05 (M34, M51, M83) binding to RNase A was determined from VHH binding in the yeast display format.
The Kd value for the epitope specific VHH cAb-RN05 clone 7 binding to RNase A was determined from VHH binding in the yeast display format.
The Kd value for the epitope specific VHH cAb-RN05 clone 22 binding to RNase A was determined from VHH binding in the yeast display format.

The affinity of epitope-specific antibody VHH#24 for binding to RNase A at the permissive pH, 7.4, was determined by isothermal titration calorimetry. On decreasing the pH, the observed binding constant decreased by about 100-fold over a range of 2 pH units.

The binding affinity of epitope-specific VHH(metal) antibody for RNAase A was determined by isothermal titration calorimetry. Reverting VHH(metal) residue H110 back to its original wild-type anti-RNase A VHH Gln residue demonstrated that H110 conferred a significant energetic penalty towards RNase A binding relative to wild-type Q110, despite the fact that H110 forms a hydrogen bond with RNase A.
